title_options: How Strong Were T. rex's Tiny Arms? 🦖
facts: Carpenter & Smith 2001 (Mesozoic Vertebrate Life): the biceps of Tyrannosaurus alone could flex about 1,955 N, roughly 199 kg per arm (a calculated estimate from the arm bones and muscle attachments); the short, stiff arm was a stable platform, possibly for clutching struggling prey.
Padian 2022, Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 67, 'Why tyrannosaurid forelimbs were so short': one hypothesis is that the forelimbs shrank to avoid injury when several adults fed on one carcass.
200 kg is about three adults of 70 kg.
description: Those tiny T. rex arms may have curled about 200 kilos each. Here's how scientists worked it out, and one idea for why they were so short. #shorts #dinosaurs #TRex #Science
sources: Carpenter & Smith 2001, in Mesozoic Vertebrate Life (Indiana University Press); Padian 2022, Acta Palaeontologica Polonica 67 (doi:10.4202/app.00921.2021).

scenes.narration: Those tiny T. rex arms may have curled about two hundred kilos each.
That's like lifting three grown adults with one small arm.
Scientists worked it out from the arm bones and the marks where its biceps attached.
So why were they so short? One idea: when several T. rex fed together, long arms would get bitten.
Short, strong arms could still grip, while staying out of the way of all those teeth.
So what do you think those little arms were really for?
